title: Jesus, My Lord, I Cry to Thee
description: Jesus, My Lord, I Cry to Thee in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 409.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, my Lord, I cry to thee A-gainst the spirit un-clean; I want a con-stant lib-er-ty, A per-fect rest from sin.

lines: Jesus, my Lord, I cry to thee
Expel the fiend out of my heart,
Now, now command him to depart,
Thy killing and thy quickening power,
The life of nature from this hour,
Then, then, my utmost Saviour, raise
To serve thy will, and spread thy praise,
This moment I thy truth confess;
The heavenly gift, the dew of grace,
The next, and every moment, Lord,
And bless me, who believe thy word,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
